name: Laboratory safety protocols and risk assessment

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of conducting a risk assessment before starting a practical physics experiment?
a: To identify potential hazards and determine precautions to prevent injury or accidents
To make the experiment take longer to complete
To calculate the exact cost of equipment
To decide what grade students will receive

questions.q: What action should you take immediately if you notice a frayed electrical cord on a low-voltage power supply during a circuit experiment?
a: Use tape to wrap it while it is plugged in
Report it to the teacher and do not use the equipment
Ignore it if the power light turns on
Cut the cord with scissors

questions.q: Which of the following safety symbols or hazard warnings indicates that a substance or component can cause severe burns to skin and eyes?
a: Radioactive symbol
Flammable symbol
Corrosive symbol
Fragile glassware symbol

questions.q: When heating water with an immersion heater or Bunsen burner during a thermal energy experiment, what safety precaution is essential?
a: Leave the container completely unmonitored
Hold the hot glass container with bare hands immediately after heating
Wear safety goggles and ensure the vessel is stable and secure
Boil the water until the container melts entirely

questions.q: Why is it important to ensure your hands are completely dry before plugging in or operating electrical equipment in the school laboratory?
a: To prevent electric shock, as water can conduct electricity
To keep the plastic casing clean of fingerprints
To prevent the equipment from overheating
To stop the wires from melting

questions.q: What is the correct way to smell a chemical or substance if required during a combined science investigation?
a: Place your nose directly over the container and inhale deeply
Gently wave your hand over the container toward your nose (wafting)
Heat the container strongly and breathe in the fumes
Taste a small drop on your finger

questions.q: If a glass beaker is accidentally knocked over and shatters on the laboratory floor, what should you do first?
a: Pick up the large pieces with bare hands immediately
Vacuum the room without telling anyone
Inform the teacher right away and keep away from the broken glass
Sweep the glass under the lab bench

questions.q: Which of the following describes a safe practice when working with optical lasers or ray boxes in light experiments?
a: Look directly into the laser beam to check its brightness
Shine the laser beam into other students' eyes as a joke
Disassemble the laser housing with a screwdriver
Never direct a laser beam into anyone's eyes and avoid specular reflections into eyes

questions.q: What hazard is associated with using a stretched spring or elastic band under high tension during a forces and extension experiment?
a: It could snap suddenly and fly toward someone's face or eyes
It will generate toxic chemical fumes
It will instantly turn into liquid mercury
It will cause an electrical short circuit

questions.q: Where should heavy equipment, such as large iron stands or heavy power packs, be stored on lab benches to prevent accidents?
a: Right on the very edge of the desk so they are easy to grab
Well away from the edge, towards the middle or back of the bench
Balanced precariously on top of books
On top of electrical sockets

questions.q: When connecting electrical circuits with DC power supplies or batteries in school labs, what helps prevent overheating and short circuits?
a: Using bare uninsulated copper wires touching wooden desks
Keeping circuits closed for hours unattended
Checking the circuit layout and having the teacher check it before turning on the power
Using the highest possible voltage setting immediately

questions.q: Why must long hair and loose clothing be tied back or secured when working near open flames or moving mechanical apparatus?
a: To look professional for school inspections
To make it easier to put on safety goggles
To keep hair cool
To prevent hair or clothing from catching fire or getting caught in moving parts

questions.q: What is the correct procedure if a small chemical splash gets into a student's eyes during a lab session?
a: Flush the eye immediately with an eyewash station or running water and notify the teacher
Rub the eye firmly with a dry cloth
Cover the eye tightly with a bandage and continue working
Ignore it until the lesson ends

questions.q: Which safety measure is crucial when carrying hot objects, such as metal blocks used in specific heat capacity experiments?
a: Use bare hands quickly so you do not drop them
Use appropriate heat-resistant gloves or tongs and place them on a heatproof mat
Blow on them while running across the room
Throw them into a sink of cold water immediately

questions.q: What does a 'fragile equipment' label on glassware like thin measuring cylinders or lenses remind students to do?
a: Store them in direct sunlight
Heat them with an intense direct flame
Handle them with care to avoid breakage and cuts
Drop them onto carpet to test durability

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of wearing safety glasses or goggles during physics experiments involving projectiles, springs, or glass?
a: To improve night vision in dark rooms
To protect eyes from UV sunlight
To magnify small objects on the bench
To protect eyes from flying debris, shattering glass, or snapping wires

questions.q: Why should food and drinks never be brought into or consumed inside a science laboratory?
a: To prevent accidental ingestion of harmful substances or contamination
Because food makes desks sticky
To stop students from talking
Because school rules forbid sitting down

questions.q: How should radioactive sources (if used in specialized advanced demonstrations) be handled safely?
a: Kept in an open tray near student faces
Handled using long tongs, for minimum time, and kept in shielded containers
Stored in ordinary pencil cases
Carried around the classroom to show friends

questions.q: What should you do with a radioactive or hazardous waste warning sign on equipment or containers?
a: Scratch it off with a pen
Ignore it if the experiment looks fun
Follow all handling instructions associated with that specific warning symbol
Throw the container in the regular paper recycling bin

questions.q: What is the safest way to disconnect a plug from a wall socket after completing an electrical experiment?
a: Pull the flexible cord as hard as possible from across the room
Jerk the wire sharply upwards
Stand on the wire to pull it free
Grip the molded plug firmly and pull straight out (never pull by the flexible cord)

questions.q: Why is it important to clear bags, coats, and stools away from lab walkways during practical lessons?
a: To prevent tripping hazards that could cause injuries or spills
To make the floor look tidy for photographs
To increase room temperature
To improve Wi-Fi signal strength

questions.q: If a student feels unwell or experiences a minor burn from touching a hot tripod, what is the immediate first aid step?
a: Apply cooking oil to the burn
Cool the burn under cold running tap water for at least 10 minutes and inform the teacher
Wrap the burn tightly in cotton wool
Apply ink to the skin

questions.q: What precaution should be taken when setting up a pendulum or mass-on-a-string experiment to ensure it does not cause injury?
a: Swing it directly toward other students' faces
Use razor-sharp steel wire
Ensure the mass is securely attached and swing it in a clear area away from passersby
Attach a heavy bowling ball to a thin sewing thread

questions.q: Which of these actions represents a severe breach of laboratory safety rules?
a: Following instructions on the worksheet
Wearing safety goggles during heating
Cleaning up your workstation before leaving
Running, horseplay, or unauthorized experimentation in the lab

questions.q: When assembling apparatus like a retort stand, clamp, and pendulum bob, why is it important to check that the clamp is tightened securely?
a: To prevent heavy apparatus from slipping or falling during the experiment
To increase the electrical voltage of the stand
To make the metal shiny
To improve sound resonance

questions.q: What should you do if an electrical appliance starts smoking or emitting a burning smell during an experiment?
a: Blow on it to cool it down
Immediately switch off the power supply at the mains or socket, and inform the teacher
Pour a beaker of water over it while plugged in
Wait to see if the smell goes away

questions.q: Why are non-slip mats or stable bases used underneath equipment like ripple tanks or heavy dynamics tracks?
a: To make the equipment heavier
To absorb sound waves
To prevent apparatus from sliding off the desk during operation
To conduct electricity

questions.q: What is the correct procedure for disposing of broken glass or sharp metal pins in the lab?
a: Throw them into regular waste paper bins
Leave them on the floor for the cleaner
Put them in student pencil cases
Place them in a designated rigid sharps or broken glass bin

questions.q: Why is it necessary to keep water away from electrical power packs and bare plug sockets?
a: To reduce the risk of short circuits, equipment damage, and electric shock
Because water dissolves plastic wires instantly
To keep the desks dry
To prevent water from evaporating

questions.q: What type of footwear is required during practical science lessons in a school laboratory?
a: Open-toe sandals
Fully enclosed, flat shoes that protect the feet
High-heeled fashion shoes
Bare feet for better balance

questions.q: If an experiment requires heating a liquid in a test tube using a Bunsen burner, which way should the mouth of the test tube point?
a: Straight down toward your feet
Directly at your lab partner's face
Away from yourself and everyone else
Straight up toward the ceiling

questions.q: What is the primary role of student safety rules in the school laboratory?
a: To restrict learning opportunities
To make experiments boring
To eliminate all fun activities
To create a safe working environment where everyone can investigate science safely

questions.q: When measuring the extension of a spring with added masses, why should you avoid adding masses beyond the spring's elastic limit?
a: It can permanently deform or snap the spring, creating a hazard
It will cause the masses to float
It increases room air pressure
It turns the spring into a magnet

questions.q: What should be checked before using a digital top-pan balance or electronic meter in the laboratory?
a: Whether it can play music
That it is correctly zeroed (tared) and plugged in safely
That it is hot to the touch
Whether it is painted black

questions.q: Why is it important to wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water at the end of a practical science lesson?
a: To cool down from walking in the hallway
To practice hand washing techniques
To remove any residual chemical traces, dust, or microscopic hazards
To dry your hands before using phones

questions.q: What should you do immediately if the fire alarm sounds during a practical science lesson?
a: Finish measuring your last data point
Pack your bags slowly
Hide under the lab bench
Stop work immediately, turn off any gas or electrical equipment, and evacuate calmly as instructed

questions.q: How can you minimize the risk of burns when using a Bunsen burner on a luminous (yellow safety) flame?
a: Keep the yellow safety flame visible so everyone knows it is lit and do not touch the barrel
Turn off all lights in the room
Wave your hands through the flame
Leave papers right next to the base

questions.q: When setting up a circuit containing a lamp and resistors, why is it recommended to check the circuit diagram before closing the switch?
a: To make the wires look artistic
To ensure correct polarity and prevent component damage or short circuits
To calculate the speed of light
To test the room temperature

questions.q: What is the main hazard of placing glass beakers containing hot liquids near the edge of a laboratory workbench?
a: They might start glowing in the dark
They will attract dust
They could be easily knocked over, causing burns and broken glass
They will freeze solid

questions.q: What should be established before beginning any new practical investigation in the laboratory?
a: Who can leave the classroom first
Which games to play afterward
What snacks to eat
A clear understanding of the procedure, hazards, and emergency exits
